newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Political parties may have to wait for the state funding they are promised by the new constitution.

- The Land Restitution Commission, set up to investigate land claims and report to the Land Claims Court, has for the first time recommended the expropriation of privately owned land as part of the restitution process.

- Relations between government and public service unions were further strained yesterday when government negotiators confirmed a cabinet decision to end a moratoriumon on forced retrenchments on March 31.

- The mines managed by Randgold turned in their best quarterly aggregate results yet in the December quarter, boosting taxed profit 69 percent to 126.6 million rand amid plans to list African exploration arm Randgold Resources in London by next year.
- The rand hit two-month high against the dollar yesterday, reaching 4.5845 in the late trade form 4.6155 late on Friday.
- The New Straits Times Press, the largest newspaper group in Malaysia, announced yesterday that it would establish a new South African daily newspaper this year.
- Randgold, the country's sixth-largest gold producer, continued its impressive rund of results this quarter after it pushed after-tax prodit ahead to 126.6 million rand.
- The rand hit its highest level against the dollar yesterday, hitting a two-month high to trade below 4.60.
- The European Union is prepared to open its markets faster and more extensively for South African products than South Africa will have to do for Europe.
- Taiwan has a contract of 100 million rand with BMW South Africa.

- A cyclone which has wreaked havoc in Madagascar is heading towards South Africa and is expected to hit KwaZulu Natal, southern parts of the Lowveld and the southern parts of neighbouring Mozambique today.
- Police said yesterday that 14 people suspected of being stock thieves were butchered on Sunday by villagers near Lusikisiki in the Eastern Cape.
